layers.name: Clients
layers.title: Shared actions for all clients
layers.body:
The backend, external scripts and integrations, AI assistants and local coding agents use the same actions. No client needs a separate endpoint.

- Backend JavaScript with `@typo3/core/action/request`
- Any HTTP client, for example `curl`, generated OpenAPI clients and automation tools
- MCP clients, for example Claude, MCP Inspector and other AI agents

layers.name: Protocols
layers.title: Different wire formats with one model
layers.body: Every action has a JSON endpoint below `/typo3/api/`, and the type of the action sets the HTTP method. TYPO3 also offers the same actions as MCP tools, over HTTP or locally through `mcp:serve`, and describes the actions in an OpenAPI 3.1 document at `/typo3/api/schema`.

layers.name: Access
layers.title: User identification and app limits
layers.body:
Every call runs as a backend user. In the backend, the session identifies the user. External applications authenticate with a token from **EXT:hub**, through OAuth 2.0 or as a static token.

**Scopes** limit the actions that an application can call for the user, for example `content:read` or `dashboard:write`.

layers.name: Action core
layers.title: Central checks and invocation
layers.body:
The core knows every action and its JSON Schema. TYPO3 compiles the actions and the schemas once with the dependency injection container. For each call, the core does these steps:

- check the needed scopes
- validate the arguments and convert them to PHP types
- call the action method with an `ActionContext`
- validate the result against the output schema
- map declared errors to status codes

layers.name: Actions
layers.title: PHP methods with #[AsAction]
layers.body:
Actions are methods of regular services with the attribute `#[AsAction]`. An action contains only the business logic, without request parsing, serialization or authentication.

TYPO3 ships actions for the dashboard, the page tree, file resources and records. The MCP server is also an action. Extensions add more actions.

layers.name: TYPO3
layers.title: Regular TYPO3 APIs
layers.body:
Actions use the regular TYPO3 APIs. Because actions run as a backend user, page permissions, table and field access, workspaces and all other backend rules apply as in the backend.

TYPO3 derives the record schemas from `TcaSchema`, so the schemas describe the content model of each installation.

steps.title: Request from the page tree
steps.body:
The page tree component calls the action with the JavaScript client:

```javascript
action('/page/tree', { … }).get()
```

The client adds a bearer token from the backend document.

steps.title: HTTP request
steps.body: `GET /typo3/api/page/tree` matches the backend route that TYPO3 registered for the action.

steps.title: Identification of the editor
steps.body:
The session cookie and the bearer token must belong to the same user, so other websites cannot call actions in the name of a logged-in editor.

TYPO3 grants all scopes that the editor can hold.

steps.title: Scope and argument checks
steps.body: The action needs `content:read`, and the editor has this scope. TYPO3 validates the query arguments against the input schema.

steps.title: Invocation
steps.body: TYPO3 converts the arguments to PHP types and calls the method with an `ActionContext`. The `ActionContext` holds the user, the scopes and the request.

steps.title: Business logic
steps.body: The page tree action builds the tree items. The action knows nothing about HTTP.

steps.title: Backend permissions
steps.body: The tree contains only the pages that the editor can see.

steps.title: Validated JSON
steps.body: TYPO3 validates the result against the output schema and returns the result as JSON. The former internal AJAX route is no longer necessary.

steps.title: Call from an integration
steps.body:
```shell
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  https://example.org/typo3/api/dashboards
```

An administrator created the token for the app in the API Hub module.

steps.title: Same route as in the backend
steps.body: The request reaches the same route as a request from the backend UI.

steps.title: Token validation by EXT:hub
steps.body: There is no backend session, so EXT:hub validates the token. The app must be enabled, and the secret of the app must be unchanged. EXT:hub loads the backend user that the app record selects.

steps.title: Scopes of the app
steps.body: The app gets exactly the scopes that the app record selects, for example `dashboard:read`.

steps.title: Scope check
steps.body: The action needs `dashboard:read`, and the app has this scope. TYPO3 rejects a write action with `403 Missing scope`.

steps.title: Invocation as the app user
steps.body: The `ActionContext` contains the backend user of the app.

steps.title: Same code as in the backend
steps.body: The dashboard action that serves the backend UI also serves the integration.

steps.title: JSON response
steps.body: The integration receives the validated JSON result.

steps.title: Connection of an AI client
steps.body: The MCP client discovers the authorization server at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` and starts the OAuth flow.

steps.title: Consent of the user
steps.body: The user logs in and approves the requested scopes on the consent screen. The token contains only the scopes that the app requested, that an administrator configured for the app and that the user can hold.

steps.title: MCP endpoint
steps.body:
```text
POST /typo3/api/mcp
{"method": "tools/list", …}
```

steps.title: Token check on every request
steps.body: EXT:hub validates the token and intersects the scopes of the token with the current scopes of the app.

steps.title: Scope mcp
steps.body: The MCP server is an action and needs the scope `mcp`.

steps.title: Tool list
steps.body: The method `tools/list` returns every action with granted scopes, with the input and output schema and hints such as `readOnlyHint`.

steps.title: Tool call
steps.body:
```json
{"method": "tools/call",
 "params": {"name": "fetch_dashboards"}}
```

steps.title: Nested invocation
steps.body: The action `mcp` calls the target action through the same `ActionInvoker`, with the same user and the same scopes.

steps.title: Third consumer of the action
steps.body: The dashboard action now serves the backend, integrations and AI agents.

steps.title: Structured result
steps.body: TYPO3 returns the validated result as `structuredContent` in the JSON-RPC response. The agent can render the dashboard of the user.

steps.title: Start of a local agent
steps.body:
```shell
vendor/bin/typo3 mcp:serve --user=editor
```

The MCP client starts the command and talks to the command through standard input and output.

steps.title: No web server
steps.body: The client and TYPO3 exchange JSON-RPC messages line by line. EXT:hub is not necessary.

steps.title: Selected user
steps.body: The user `editor` must exist and be enabled. TYPO3 grants all scopes that the user `editor` can hold. Without `--user`, TYPO3 uses the CLI user `_cli_`.

steps.title: Same MCP implementation
steps.body: The same MCP action handles `initialize`, `tools/list` and `tools/call`.

steps.title: Same validation
steps.body: TYPO3 invokes and validates tool calls exactly as over HTTP.

steps.title: Permissions of the user
steps.body: The agent can do what `editor` can do, and nothing more.
